***Achievement establishes complete amino acid detection as a new benchmark for single-molecule protein sequencing***


***Capability is expected to lay the foundation for reference-free protein identification and expanded analysis of proteoforms***


BRANFORD, Conn., Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Quantum-Si Incorporated (Nasdaq: QSI) (“Quantum-Si,” “QSI” or the “Company”), a proteomics technology company redefining protein analysis through single-molecule protein sequencing, today announced that it has demonstrated detection of all 20 naturally occurring amino acids in its Proteus development program, achieving its year-end 2026 goal ahead of schedule. The Company believes complete amino acid detection can expand the information obtained directly from individual protein molecules and establish the technical foundation for increasingly comprehensive protein identification, including reference-free approaches.


Proteins are constructed from an alphabet of 20 amino acids. Just as reading DNA sequences depends on distinguishing each of its four nucleotide bases, reading protein sequence requires distinguishing the full 20 amino acid alphabet. The Company believes detection of all 20 amino acids will become a foundational performance benchmark for protein sequencing technologies seeking to identify proteins and resolve meaningful sequence variation directly.


“Proteins contain an alphabet of 20 amino acids, and for the first time, we have demonstrated the ability to detect that complete alphabet at the single-molecule level,” said Jeff Hawkins, President and Chief Executive Officer. “We believe this is an important moment not only for Quantum-Si, but for the emerging field of protein sequencing. From this point forward, the question should not simply be whether a technology can generate information from a protein. The standard should increasingly be whether it can distinguish the full amino acid alphabet needed to read protein sequence and variation comprehensively.”


Hawkins continued, “The history of genomics shows that when scientists gain more complete access to biological sequence information, the impact can extend far beyond the initial instrument or application. Complete amino acid detection creates a foundation for reference-free protein identification and, over time, could open new approaches to studying proteoforms, sequence variants, post-translational modifications, engineered proteins and previously uncharacterized biology. We continue to focus on doing the work required to translate this achievement into a high-performing commercial product, but the significance of reaching all 20 amino acids should not be understated.”


Quantum-Si is now working to incorporate 20 amino acid detection into a developmental sequencing kit for use on Proteus instruments. As that work progresses, the Company expects to share additional data demonstrating continued improvements in Proteus performance and progress toward commercial launch.


*Figure 1: The 20 amino acids that make up proteins, grouped by side-chain chemistry. Quantum-Si has now demonstrated detection of all 20 in its Proteus development program.*


**About Quantum-Si Incorporated** Quantum-Si is transforming proteomics with a benchtop platform that brings single-molecule protein analysis to every lab, everywhere. The Company’s platform enables real-time kinetic-based detection and allows researchers to move beyond traditional, multistep workflows and directly access dynamic, functional protein insights with unparalleled resolution. By making protein analysis simpler, faster, and more informative, Quantum-Si is accelerating proteomic discoveries to improve the way we live.
